extracted.intended_audience: Scientists invited to referee manuscripts for Cell Research (cell and molecular biology journal)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for peer reviewers/referees assessing manuscripts submitted to the journal Cell Research, covering criteria for publication, report structure and content, confidentiality, conflicts of interest, timing, and editorial interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong evidence for conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must provide strong evidence for the conclusions that are drawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees should assess whether data and analyses adequately support the claims; look for technical or interpretational weaknesses that undermine conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: The work must be novel (abstracts, meeting reports and www preprints are not considered to compromise novelty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check prior literature and preprints to ensure claims are new; consider whether similar results have been reported elsewhere and whether novelty is sufficient for the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad biological significance
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript should have broad biological significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether findings will be of interest beyond a narrow technical audience and whether they advance understanding in biology more generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance to the specific field
rubrics_metrics.description: The work should be important to the specific field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the relevance and expected impact within the subfield; determine whether the paper addresses an important question or fills a significant gap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit to journal scope and general interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors screen submissions for suitability for review based on scope and likelihood to meet editorial criteria; only manuscripts judged most likely to meet criteria are sent for formal review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees should consider whether the topic fits Cell Research's scope and is of sufficient general interest when evaluating and recommending; note to editors if scope mismatch is apparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Referee selection is based on expertise, reputation, specific recommendations, and previous experience; avoid using referees who are chronically slow, sloppy, too harsh or too lenient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors choose referees with relevant technical expertise and appropriate reviewing record; potential referees should accept only if they can review promptly and conscientiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate actions on receiving a manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt referees should: double-check the deadline, read the editor's letter for specific points to address, skim the manuscript for conflicts of interest, and consider whether the topic fits the journal and is of sufficient general interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the editorial office immediately if you cannot meet the deadline or if you identify a conflict; ensure you understand any specific questions the editor has asked you to consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts refereed for Cell Research should be treated as strictly confidential and not discussed with anyone not directly involved in the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If colleagues are consulted they must be identified to the editors; check with editors before consulting experts outside your lab to avoid excluded individuals; avoid disclosing your identity to authors—if you wish to reveal identity do so via the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of referee reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Referee reports should provide the editors with the information needed to reach a decision and instruct authors on how to strengthen their manuscript if revision is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance information for editorial decision-making with constructive guidance for authors; be specific about weaknesses and how to address them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division between author-facing and confidential comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees are asked to submit both confidential comments to the editor and comments that can be directly transmitted to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve recommendations about publication and other confidential judgements for the confidential section; author-facing comments should focus on constructive criticism and improvement without confidential recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and language of reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a positive and impartial, but critical, attitude; criticisms should remain dispassionate and offensive language is not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ad hominem or inflammatory phrasing; concentrate on objective critique of data, interpretation and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial summary paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: The ideal report should include an initial paragraph that summarises the major findings and the referee's overall impressions, as well as highlighting major shortcomings of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise overview up front so editors and authors immediately grasp the paper's main contributions and key problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific numbered comments with major/minor distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Include specific numbered comments, which may be broken down into major and minor criticisms if appropriate; numbering facilitates the editor's evaluation and the authors' rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear numbering and label items as major or minor to help authors prioritize revisions and to help editors weigh the issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key substantive questions the report should answer
rubrics_metrics.description: The report should answer: what are the major claims and how significant are they? are the claims novel and convincing? are the claims appropriately discussed in the context of earlier literature? who will be interested and why? does the paper stand out in some way from others in its field? are there other experiments that would strengthen the paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly address these questions in the report where applicable; justify your evaluations with evidence from the manuscript or literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice for manuscripts meriting further consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: For manuscripts that may merit further consideration, referees should advise on how clarity of writing might be improved, how the manuscript might be shortened, how to do the study justice without overselling the claims, how to represent earlier literature more fairly, and how to improve presentation of methodological detail so experiments can be reproduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete suggestions (e.g., sections to shorten, figures to combine, specific text revisions, methodological details to add) rather than vague comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include publication recommendation in author-facing report
rubrics_metrics.description: This author report should not include a recommendation regarding publication, which is regarded as confidential information since the final decision rests with the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place any recommendation to accept/major revision/minor revision/reject in the confidential comments to the editor only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential evaluation metrics (rating relative to others)
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript should be rated relative to others in the field on: Originality and importance; Technical quality; Clarity of presentation — using categories Top 10% / Top 20% / Top 50% / Lower 50%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide one of the percentile bands for each axis and justify the placement if necessary; these comparative judgments help editors calibrate decisions across submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional confidential comments to the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential comments may include a definite recommendation regarding publication, an assessment of how much suggested additional experiments would improve the manuscript and how difficult they would be to complete within a reasonable timeframe (1–2 months), and whether the study is sufficiently promising to encourage resubmission in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give pragmatic advice about feasibility and impact of additional work, and whether resubmission after major new experiments would be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing of referee reports by editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors do not suppress referee reports; almost always any comments intended for authors are transmitted. On rare occasions they may edit a report to correct an obvious factual mistake, or to remove offensive language or comments that reveal confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid making factual errors or including identifiable/confidential material; use professional language to minimize need for editorial edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees should respond promptly or inform the editorial office if they anticipate significant delays to allow finding alternative referees and to keep authors informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot meet the deadline, notify editors immediately with an expected timeframe or decline to allow timely handling of the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest — when to decline or declare
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors try to avoid referees who have recent or ongoing collaborations with the authors, have commented on drafts of the manuscript, are in direct competition, have a history of dispute with the authors, or have a financial interest in the outcome. Referees should draw attention to anything that might affect their report (including commercial interests) and decline to referee if they feel unable to be objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt, disclose possible conflicts to the editor; note that prior review of the paper for another journal is not a reason to decline per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alert editors to publication policy and ethical concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees who are familiar with the field are more likely to recognise breaches of publication policy or ethical conduct (such as plagiarism or author conflict of interest) and should alert the editors to any potential problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report suspected ethical issues in the confidential comments to the editor with supporting evidence; do not make public accusations in author-facing comments.
